statement_record.book: For an object C of a locally small category, Hom_C(-,C) : C^op ⟶ Sets sends an object A to the hom-set Hom(A,C) and an arrow f : A → B to the precomposition map f* : Hom(B,C) → Hom(A,C), f*(h) = h ∘ f.
statement_record.intree: Curried_Hom `(C : Category) : C^op ⟶ [C, Sets] with fmap f acting by (fun g => g ∘ op f); Curried_CoHom C := Curried_Hom C^op : C ⟶ [C^op, Sets], written [Hom ─ , A], so [Hom ─,A] : C^op ⟶ Sets has fobj a = hom C a A and fmap f h = h ∘ f. The bifunctor Hom C : C^op ∏ C ⟶ Sets acts by (fun g => snd f ∘ g ∘ fst f), i.e. precomposition in the contravariant slot.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same — the setoid rephrasing (hom-sets are setoid objects of Sets, equality of maps is ≈) is faithful, and functoriality is proved rather than asserted. statement_record.book: If G is a group object in a locally small category C, the contravariant representable Hom_C(-,G) carries a group structure on each hom-set (pointwise unit, product and inverse), so it lifts to a functor C^op ⟶ Grp over the Sets-valued representable; precomposition h* : Hom(X,G) → Hom(Y,G) is a group homomorphism.
statement_record.intree: Hom_Monoid {x} `(Y : Monoid y) : @MonoidObject C CC_Monoidal (y ^ x) — the INTERNAL hom y^x of a cartesian closed C carries the pointwise monoid structure of a monoid object y. statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: three separate weakenings. (1) The structure transferred is a MONOID structure, not a group — there is no Hom_Group / no analogue of Hom_Monoid for GroupObject anywhere in the tree (grep -rn 'Hom_Group|GroupHom' -> 0 hits). (3) Hom_Monoid is a single object-level instance: there is no functor C^op ⟶ Mon (nor ⟶ Grp), and nothing asserts that precomposition h* is a monoid/group homomorphism, which is the functoriality half of the example.
